2610.03574.title: HyperBrowseComp: A Multilingual and Multimodal Stress Test for Web-Browsing Agents
2610.03574.paper_summary: We introduce HyperBrowseComp, a multilingual and multimodal browsing benchmark comprising 423 manually authored and human-validated questions across 13 languages, written by native or highly proficient speakers. Questions are designed to be extremely challenging. Each question targets a concise, publicly verifiable answer whose discovery requires locating obscure evidence, following multi-step clue chains, or inspecting heterogeneous sources such as videos, scanned documents, images, or maps. Easier questions are filtered out by evaluating them with models without internet access to reduce the likelihood that they can be answered with parametric knowledge alone. We evaluate several models using provider-native search and a shared external retrieval harness under a common agent protocol. To contextualize model performance and effort, we also conduct a human evaluation on a sample of the questions. HyperBrowseComp provides a challenging testbed for persistent information seeking across languages and evidence modalities, with difficulty arising from discovering and connecting evidence on the open web.
2610.03574.paper_summary_zh: 我們介紹 HyperBrowseComp，這是一個多語言和多模態的瀏覽基準，包含423個手動編寫並經過人類驗證的問題，涵蓋13種語言，這些問題由母語或高水平的說話者撰寫。問題設計得極具挑戰性。每個問題的目標是找到一個簡潔且可公開驗證的答案，其發現需要定位晦澀的證據、跟隨多步驟的線索鏈，或檢查異質來源，如視頻、掃描文件、圖像或地圖。較簡單的問題通過使用無法訪問互聯網的模型進行評估來過濾，以減少僅用參數知識回答的可能性。我們使用提供者本地搜索和共享外部檢索工具在共同代理協議下評估幾個模型。為了對模型性能和努力進行背景化，我們還對問題樣本進行了人類評估。HyperBrowseComp 提供了一個具有挑戰性的測試平台，用於跨語言和證據模態的持續信息尋求，挑戰來自於在開放網絡上發現和連接證據。
